'''Julie Grollier''' is a [[French people|French]] [[physicist]] working in the field of [[spintronics]]. She won the Irène Joliot-Curie Prize from the French Academy of Sciences in 2021.<ref>[https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/personne/julie-grollier Julie Grollier profile] – CNRS</ref>

== Education and career ==
Grollier studied<ref>[https://www.weforum.org/people/julie-grollier Julie Grollier] – World Economic Forum</ref> at the French engineering school [[Supélec]], before doing an internship in the Laboratory of Crystallography and Materials Science at the [[University of Caen Normandy]]. She then conducted her doctoral research at [[École normale supérieure Paris-Saclay]] under the supervision of [[Nobel Prize]] laureate [[Albert Fert]], working on magnetization reversal by the injection of spin-current injection. She later joined the [[University of Groningen]] in the [[Netherlands]] and then the [[Centre for Nanosciences and Nanotechnologies]] (formerly known as Institut d'électronique fondamentale, in [[France]]), as a postdoctoral fellow working on the magnetization dynamics of nano-magnets. She joined the [[Joint Research Unit|joint research unit]] {{ill|CNRS/Thales|fr|Unité mixte de physique CNRS/Thales}} in 2005.<ref>[http://www.cnrs-thales.fr/spip.php?article59&lang=fr Julie Grollier] – Unité mixte de physique CNRS/Thales</ref>

==Recognition==
Grollier was awarded the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2018,<ref>[https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/82-nouveaux-talents-du-cnrs 82 Nouveaux talents du CNRS] – CNRS</ref> and the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2021.<ref>[https://twitter.com/AcadSciences/status/1463148733009481728 Académie de Sciences] – Twitter</ref>

In 2015, she was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS), after a nomination from the APS Topical Group on Magnetism and its Applications, "for measurements of spin-transfer torque dynamics and the development of devices to implement biologically inspired computing".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2015&unit_id=GMAG&institution=|title=Fellows nominated in 2015 by the Topical Group on Magnetism and its Applications|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2021-11-29}}</ref>
